_meta.indication: STRENSIQ is a tissue nonspecific alkaline phosphatase indicated for the treatment of patients with perinatal/infantile- and juvenile-onset hypophosphatasia (HPP)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ENB-002-08/ENB-003-08 and ENB-010-10 (perinatal/infantile-onset HPP pivotal trials), with ENB-011-10 natural history study as historical control
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label single-arm trials in treated patients compared with a non-concurrent retrospective natural history (historical) control cohort
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with perinatal/infantile-onset HPP younger than 3 years and 5 years old, respectively
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (primary efficacy endpoint for the perinatal/infantile-onset HPP indication)
pivotal_trials.n: 68 treated patients included in survival analyses vs 48 natural history control patients
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 504 (9.6 years), 62 of 68 (91%) treated patients survived vs 13 of 48 (27%) historical control patients; ventilator-free survival for the pooled population was approximately 80%

nct_ctgov.title: Open-Label Study of Asfotase Alfa in Infants and Children ≤ 5 Years of Age With Hypophosphatasia (HPP)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ENB-006-09/ENB-008-10 (juvenile-onset HPP pivotal trial), with ALX-HPP-502s natural history study as historical control
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label trial in 13 pediatric patients 5 years and older compared with a retrospective historical control group
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients 5 years and older with juvenile-onset HPP
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in gait measured by the modified Performance Oriented Mobility Assessment-Gait (mPOMA-G) scale (primary efficacy endpoint for the juvenile-onset HPP indication)
pivotal_trials.n: 8 treated patients vs 6 historical control patients
pivotal_trials.result: Mean rate of change in mPOMA-G score for treated patients was 2.25 per year; however the review team deemed this primary analysis for the juvenile-onset population was not robust from a statistical perspective and was insufficient as stand-alone evidence to support efficacy. Supportive growth data showed mean change in height z-score of 0.6 for treated vs 0 for controls, and mean change in weight z-score of 1.1 for treated vs 0.2 for controls

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions (63%), lipodystrophy (28%), ectopic calcifications (14%), and hypersensitivity reactions (12%). Most serious risks are life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis
target_moa: Asfotase alfa is a recombinant fusion glycoprotein incorporating the catalytic domain of human tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNSALP), the Fc domain of human IgG1, and a bone-targeting deca-aspartate domain; it replaces the deficient TNSALP enzyme that mineralizes bone by cleaving inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi)
modality: enzyme (recombinant tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase Fc-fusion enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS INCLUDING ANAPHYLAXIS — anaphylaxis has occurred during the early course and after extended duration of therapy; if a severe hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue STRENSIQ and immediately initiate appropriate medical treatment including epinephrine

rems.type: No REMS; potential safety risks can be communicated by labeling and a REMS is not necessary

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meetings were held regarding this application

description.text: Labeling update with long-term efficacy and safety data from completed studies and postmarketing reports; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for an update to the product labeling based on long-term efficacy and safety data from patients treated in Study 1 (ENB-002-08), Study 2 (ENB-010-10), and Study 3 (ENB-006-09/ENB-008-10), which were completed after the original BLA approval, as well as labeling updates based on postmarketing reports..

summary.text: STRENSIQ received Orphan Drug Designation (September 12, 2008), Fast Track Designation (May 14, 2009), and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (May 21, 2013), and was reviewed under Priority Review. It was approved as the first therapy for perinatal/infantile- and juvenile-onset HPP based on comparisons of treated patients to natural history cohorts, and HPP was determined to be eligible for a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher

citations.quote: Asfotase alfa received Orphan Drug Designation on September 12, 2008, Fast Track Designation on May 14, 2009, and Breakthrough Designation for the perinatal/infantile and juvenile forms of HPP on May 21, 2013.
This BLA was reviewed as a Priority Review; because of a Major Amendment, the PDUFA deadline was extended from August 23, to November 23, 2015.
Strensiq will be the first approved therapy for the indication of perinatal/infantile and juvenile-onset HPP, a devastating childhood condition for which there is no effective treatment.
The Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD) has reviewed this request and concluded that HPP meets the FDASIA definition of a rare pediatric disease, and is eligible for a voucher.

requirement.text: PMR 2949-1: Conduct a prospective, long-term observational study in STRENSIQ-treated patients with perinatal/infantile-onset and juvenile-onset HPP from birth and older to assess long-term safety (severe hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, systemic immune complex-mediated reactions, and ectopic calcification events), following patients a minimum of 5 years from the time of enrollment, or until death, whichever comes first

citations.quote: Conduct a prospective, long-term, observational study in STRENSIQ (asfotase alfa) treated patients with perinatal/infantile-onset and juvenile-onset hypophosphatasia (HPP) from ages birth and older. The purpose of the study is to assess the long term safety of treatment with STRENSIQ (asfotase alfa) with respect to incidence rates of severe hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis), systemic immune complex-mediated reactions and ectopic calcification events.
Enroll adequate number of patients, including both infantile-onset and juvenile-onset-patients, and follow for a minimum of 5 years from the time of enrollment, or until death, whichever comes first.

requirement.text: PMR 2949-2: Develop an assay to directly compare the complement activating capacity of STRENSIQ (asfotase alfa) to that of human IgG1

citations.quote: Develop an assay to directly compare the complement activating capacity of STRENSIQ (asfotase) alfa to that of human IgG1. The assay should be set up under conditions to readily detect complement activation by IgG1.

requirement.text: PMC 2949-3: Develop a validated cross-reactive immunologic material (CRIM) assay for HPP patients and test samples in a cohort of untreated patients, correlated with antibody response, genetic mutations, enzyme activity and clinical outcome

citations.quote: Develop a validated cross-reactive immunologic material (CRIM) assay for patients with hypophosphatasia (HPP) and test patient samples in a cohort of untreated patients. Results should be correlated with antibody response (binding and neutralizing), genetic mutations, enzyme activity level and clinical outcome in patients who are receiving STRENSIQ (asfotase alfa) treatment.
